scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets.purpose: The RealPage Fixed Assets application: the subledger that holds every capitalized asset of a property — buildings, building improvements (roofs, HVAC, unit renovations), land improvements, appliances and FF&E — with its cost, class, in-service date and depreciation schedule, and that posts depreciation to the GL.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets.outcome: A single asset register per property that supports the largest balance-sheet balance in multifamily (net real estate) and drives monthly depreciation in the GAAP and tax books.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets.rootCause: Institutional multifamily owners spend heavily on capital programs (value-add unit interiors at $8K-$15K per unit, roofs, parking lots). GAAP requires those costs to be capitalized and depreciated asset by asset, and tax returns use different lives (MACRS). A spreadsheet register breaks down at hundreds of assets per property and is not auditable.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets.ifSkipped: Capital spend sits in GL accounts with no asset detail, depreciation is estimated rather than calculated, disposals of replaced components are never recorded, and the asset register cannot support purchase-price allocations at sale or audit testing.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-3 — capitalization vs repair (tangible property regulations)
redFlags: Capital GL accounts with balances but no assets in the register
Assets depreciating in the GAAP book with tax-book lives

scr_fixed_assets_introduction_to_fixed_a.purpose: Introduces the tabs (All, Setup), the components (asset classes, assets, draft assets, depreciation batches, reports) and the end-to-end workflow of Fixed Assets, including how capitalization policy thresholds (e.g., > $2,500 and useful life > 1 year) decide what becomes an asset.
scr_fixed_assets_introduction_to_fixed_a.outcome: Accountants understand how an invoice becomes an asset and how that asset becomes monthly depreciation before touching live data.
scr_fixed_assets_introduction_to_fixed_a.rootCause: Most fixed-asset errors come from not understanding the flow: capitalizing below the threshold, bypassing asset creation by coding invoices straight to 1530, or posting depreciation before activating drafts. The introduction exists to prevent those structural mistakes.
scr_fixed_assets_introduction_to_fixed_a.ifSkipped: New accountants capitalize routine repairs, miss drafts, and create register-to-GL breaks that take months to unwind.
gaap: Treas. Reg. §1.263(a)-1(f) — de minimis safe harbor ($2,500 per invoice/item without AFS)
redFlags: Staff unaware of the owner's capitalization threshold

scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_all_tab.purpose: The All tab of Fixed Assets, grouping the day-to-day menus: Search & Find (Assets, Draft Assets), Periodic Tasks (Post Depreciation) and Reports (Asset Info, Asset Reconciliation).
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_all_tab.outcome: Accountants reach every operational fixed-asset task — adding, activating, depreciating, reconciling — from one tab.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_all_tab.rootCause: The monthly fixed-asset routine (activate drafts, post depreciation, reconcile) spans several menus. Grouping them on one tab supports doing them in the correct order during close.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_all_tab.ifSkipped: Accountants miss one step in the routine, most often the reconciliation after depreciation.
redFlags: Depreciation posted but reconciliation report never run

scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_setup_tab.purpose: The Setup tab where asset classes are configured — the depreciation method, useful life, GL accounts and books (GAAP, tax) that each new asset inherits.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_setup_tab.outcome: Asset classes that encode the owner's capitalization and depreciation policy, so individual assets default correctly.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_setup_tab.rootCause: Consistency of depreciation depends on consistent class settings. Setting lives and accounts once at the class level prevents each accountant choosing different lives for similar assets (e.g., 5 vs 7 years for appliances).
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_setup_tab.ifSkipped: Assets are set up with inconsistent lives and accounts, making depreciation incomparable across properties and hard to defend at audit.
redFlags: Class lives inconsistent with the owner's fixed asset policy

scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_workflow.purpose: Describes how assets flow across RealPage objects: capital invoices in A/P (or external systems like OpsTechnology) create draft assets, drafts are activated into the register, the register generates depreciation schedules, and depreciation batches post to the GL.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_workflow.outcome: A clear chain from invoice to depreciation entry that the accountant can trace for any asset.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_workflow.rootCause: Auditors test fixed assets by tracing from invoice to register to GL and back. Understanding the workflow is required to support that trace and to find where a break occurred.
scr_fixed_assets_fixed_assets_workflow.ifSkipped: Accountants cannot trace an asset back to its invoice, failing audit tests of additions.
redFlags: Assets with no source invoice reference

scr_fixed_assets_setting_up_fixed_assets.purpose: Chapter on using the Setup tab to configure Fixed Assets before live use: application configuration and asset classes aligned to the owner's capitalization policy.
scr_fixed_assets_setting_up_fixed_assets.outcome: A configured application where capital invoices produce correctly classified assets from day one.
scr_fixed_assets_setting_up_fixed_assets.rootCause: Setup decisions (classes, lives, GL mapping, books) determine every future depreciation entry. Getting them wrong means correcting many assets later, often as a change in estimate or an error correction.
scr_fixed_assets_setting_up_fixed_assets.ifSkipped: Assets inherit wrong settings and years of depreciation must be recalculated.
redFlags: Application used live before classes were reviewed

scr_fixed_assets_configuration.purpose: Configuration options for the Fixed Assets application itself — how assets integrate with A/P and other applications and default behaviors — found under the Setup tab.
scr_fixed_assets_configuration.outcome: Fixed Assets behaves consistently with the company's A/P and GL processes.
scr_fixed_assets_configuration.rootCause: Integration settings decide whether capital invoices automatically create draft assets. Without them, every capital invoice needs a manual asset, which is where additions get missed.
scr_fixed_assets_configuration.ifSkipped: Capital invoices post to asset accounts with no asset created, breaking the register-to-GL tie.
redFlags: Integration disabled while capital invoices are processed in A/P

scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes.purpose: Asset classes group assets that share depreciation and accounting rules — e.g., Building (27.5 or 40 years), Roofs (20 years), HVAC (15 years), Appliances (5 years), Flooring (5-7 years) — and automatically apply those rules to new assets.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes.outcome: Each new asset receives the correct life, method and GL accounts from its class without manual entry.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes.rootCause: A value-add program can add hundreds of similar assets per year. Class-level defaults are the only practical way to apply the owner's depreciation policy consistently and defend it to auditors.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes.ifSkipped: Lives are chosen asset by asset, leading to inconsistent depreciation and audit adjustments.
gaap: IRC §168(c) — recovery periods for tax book
redFlags: Classes with lives out of line with industry practice (e.g., 3-year roofs)
Land improvements classed with non-depreciable land

scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes_list.purpose: List of all asset classes with actions to add, view, edit and delete, used to maintain the class catalog.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes_list.outcome: A maintained class catalog that reflects the current fixed asset policy.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes_list.rootCause: Policies change (new classes for EV chargers, smart-home tech) and classes must be kept current so new asset types are not forced into ill-fitting classes.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_classes_list.ifSkipped: New asset types are misclassified into classes with wrong lives.
redFlags: Catch-all 'Other' class with many assets

scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_class.purpose: Creates a new asset class with its depreciation method (straight-line typically), useful life, convention, GL asset/accumulated depreciation/expense accounts and books.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_class.outcome: A new category of asset can be depreciated under a defined policy.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_class.rootCause: When owners introduce new capital programs (solar panels, smart locks, amenity upgrades), those assets need a defined life and accounts before they can be capitalized consistently.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_class.ifSkipped: New asset types are forced into existing classes with inappropriate lives.
gaap: IRC §168 — tax classes (e.g., 5-year for certain personal property)
redFlags: Class created without tax book settings when the owner files on MACRS

scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.purpose: Opens an asset class to review or change its settings — life, method, accounts, books.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.outcome: Class settings can be verified or corrected.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.rootCause: Editing class settings affects future assets; changes to useful life for existing assets are changes in estimate that must be applied prospectively and documented.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.ifSkipped: Wrong class settings persist, or edits are made without considering the prospective-change rule.
gaap: ASC 250-10-45-17 — change in estimate applied prospectively
redFlags: Useful life changed with retroactive recalculation (should be prospective)

scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset_class.purpose: Deletes an asset class that has no assets attached, typically one created in error or obsolete.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset_class.outcome: The class catalog stays clean; classes in use are protected from deletion.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset_class.rootCause: Unused or duplicate classes invite misclassification. The system prevents deleting classes with assets because that would orphan their depreciation settings.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset_class.ifSkipped: Duplicate classes remain and new assets are split inconsistently between them.
redFlags: Near-duplicate classes both in use

scr_fixed_assets_asset_class_page.purpose: The asset class record page: a general section summarizing the class and a books section defining depreciation settings per book (GAAP, tax, other).
scr_fixed_assets_asset_class_page.outcome: Depreciation rules are defined per book so one asset can depreciate differently for GAAP and tax.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_class_page.rootCause: Institutional owners typically need GAAP depreciation for financial statements and MACRS for partnership tax returns. Book-level settings on the class allow both from the same asset record.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_class_page.ifSkipped: Tax depreciation is calculated outside the system, creating book-tax reconciliation work each year.
redFlags: Tax book missing on classes used for tax-return depreciation

scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_book_to.purpose: Adds a depreciation book (e.g., Tax) to an existing asset class so assets in that class start calculating depreciation in the new book.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_book_to.outcome: Existing classes support an additional reporting basis without recreating assets.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_book_to.rootCause: Owners sometimes add tax-book tracking after go-live, or a new JV partner requires a different basis. Adding a book to the class extends depreciation to that basis.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_an_asset_book_to.ifSkipped: The additional basis is tracked in spreadsheets outside the register.
redFlags: Book added without catch-up depreciation for assets already in service

scr_fixed_assets_using_fixed_assets.purpose: Chapter on operating Fixed Assets day to day — finding and managing assets, activating drafts, posting depreciation and running reports — as the central location to track property capital.
scr_fixed_assets_using_fixed_assets.outcome: A repeatable monthly fixed-asset routine within the close.
scr_fixed_assets_using_fixed_assets.rootCause: Fixed assets need a monthly routine (activate, depreciate, reconcile), not a year-end cleanup. The chapter defines that routine.
scr_fixed_assets_using_fixed_assets.ifSkipped: Fixed assets are handled once a year, producing large catch-up entries and audit findings.
redFlags: No fixed-asset activity recorded for months at properties with active capital programs

scr_fixed_assets_search_and_find.purpose: The Search & Find menus (Assets, Draft Assets) used to locate assets by property, class, status or description to review, edit, transfer or dispose.
scr_fixed_assets_search_and_find.outcome: Accountants quickly locate the asset records affected by a replacement, casualty or audit question.
scr_fixed_assets_search_and_find.rootCause: When a roof is replaced or a unit burns, the accountant must find the old component in the register to dispose of it. Fast search is what makes component disposal practical.
scr_fixed_assets_search_and_find.ifSkipped: Old components are never found and disposed, inflating the register.
redFlags: Vague asset descriptions that make components impossible to find

scr_fixed_assets_assets.purpose: Assets section of the application — once classes exist, accountants create and manage individual asset records representing capitalized property components, equipment and improvements.
scr_fixed_assets_assets.outcome: Each capitalized item has an asset record with cost, class, location and in-service date.
scr_fixed_assets_assets.rootCause: Depreciation, disposal and sale allocations all depend on asset-level records; totals in the GL are not enough to support them.
scr_fixed_assets_assets.ifSkipped: Capital costs exist only as GL totals, making disposals and audits impossible to support.
redFlags: Assets without in-service dates

scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_list.purpose: List of all assets where the accountant adds assets manually or by import (including opening accumulated depreciation for acquired properties), views, edits, transfers, reclasses and disposes of them.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_list.outcome: The working register for each property, including historical assets brought over at acquisition.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_list.rootCause: Acquired properties arrive with existing asset bases (from the purchase price allocation or the prior owner's register) that must be loaded with opening accumulated depreciation to continue depreciation correctly.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_list.ifSkipped: Acquired assets are loaded without opening balances, over-depreciating or double-depreciating them.
gaap: ASC 805-50 — asset acquisitions and cost allocation
redFlags: Imported assets whose opening accumulated depreciation does not match the prior register

scr_fixed_assets_integrating_with_assets.purpose: Enables integration between A/P and RealPage Facilities (maintenance) assets so that capital items purchased through A/P link to the physical asset records maintenance teams track (e.g., an HVAC unit's serial number and location).
scr_fixed_assets_integrating_with_assets.outcome: Accounting assets and maintenance assets refer to the same physical items, supporting warranty tracking and component disposal.
scr_fixed_assets_integrating_with_assets.rootCause: Maintenance teams know which unit's water heater was replaced; accounting knows its cost. Linking them lets the accountant dispose of the right replaced component and supports lifecycle planning.
scr_fixed_assets_integrating_with_assets.ifSkipped: Replacements are capitalized without disposing of the specific old component, because accounting cannot identify it.
redFlags: Integration enabled but facilities assets not linked to accounting assets

scr_fixed_assets_adding_a_new_asset_manu.purpose: Creates an asset record directly in Fixed Assets (rather than from an A/P invoice) — cost, class, location, in-service date, description — for items like assets acquired through a JE, contributed capital or corrections.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_a_new_asset_manu.outcome: Capital items that did not come through A/P still get a register record and depreciation schedule.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_a_new_asset_manu.rootCause: Some capital costs arrive by JE (reclass of a repair to capital, capitalized interest, allocation of acquisition costs). Without a manual path, those costs sit in asset accounts without a register record.
scr_fixed_assets_adding_a_new_asset_manu.ifSkipped: Asset accounts carry costs that never depreciate, and the register never ties to the GL.
redFlags: Manual assets with no supporting JE or invoice reference
Manual asset and A/P-created draft for the same item (double capitalization)

scr_fixed_assets_importing_assets.purpose: Loads many assets at once through the Financial Suite import template — typically when onboarding an acquisition or migrating a register from Yardi or another system.
scr_fixed_assets_importing_assets.outcome: A complete opening register loaded accurately with cost and accumulated depreciation per asset.
scr_fixed_assets_importing_assets.rootCause: Acquisitions and management take-overs bring hundreds of existing assets. Manual entry is impractical and error-prone; import ensures the opening register matches the prior system and the GL.
scr_fixed_assets_importing_assets.ifSkipped: Opening registers are incomplete or keyed with errors, breaking the tie to the GL from day one.
redFlags: Imported totals not reconciled to the opening trial balance
Imported in-service dates defaulted to import date

scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.purpose: Opens an asset to view or edit its details — description, location, class, in-service date, cost — and its depreciation history.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.outcome: Asset details are verified or corrected, e.g. fixing a wrong in-service date on a completed project.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.rootCause: Asset data entered at activation is often incomplete (placeholder descriptions, invoice date as in-service date). Correcting it keeps depreciation right and supports future disposals.
scr_fixed_assets_viewing_or_editing_an_a.ifSkipped: Depreciation continues on wrong dates or classes and assets remain unidentifiable.
gaap: ASC 250 — correction of errors vs change in estimate
redFlags: In-service date edits on assets with posted depreciation without a catch-up review

scr_fixed_assets_disposing_of_assets_in_.purpose: Disposes of multiple assets at once for the same reason — property sale, casualty loss (fire, flood, hurricane) or a mass component replacement program.
scr_fixed_assets_disposing_of_assets_in_.outcome: All affected assets are derecognized in one action with a consistent disposal date and reason.
scr_fixed_assets_disposing_of_assets_in_.rootCause: Property sales and casualty events affect dozens or hundreds of assets simultaneously. Disposing one by one is slow and risks inconsistent dates across assets.
scr_fixed_assets_disposing_of_assets_in_.ifSkipped: Sold or destroyed assets linger in the register and continue depreciating.
gaap: ASC 610-20 — gains and losses on sale of nonfinancial assets
redFlags: Sold property assets still depreciating after the closing date
Casualty disposals without an insurance receivable

scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset.purpose: Permanently deletes an asset record — only appropriate for records created in error (duplicates, wrong property), never for real disposals, which must use the dispose function.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset.outcome: Erroneous asset records are removed without creating a false gain or loss.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset.rootCause: Deletion erases history, so it must be limited to records that should never have existed. Using delete for a real disposal would remove cost and accumulated depreciation without any disposal entry or audit trail.
scr_fixed_assets_deleting_an_asset.ifSkipped: Duplicate assets double-depreciate; conversely, deleting real assets destroys the audit trail.
gaap: ASC 360-10-40 — disposals must be recorded, not deleted
redFlags: Deleted assets that had posted depreciation
Deletions used instead of disposals after a sale

scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_page.purpose: The asset record page with tabs for general information (description, class, location, cost, in-service date) and depreciation settings and history by book.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_page.outcome: Complete detail for one asset to support depreciation, disposal and audit questions.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_page.rootCause: Auditors and tax preparers need asset-level cost, dates and depreciation to test additions and compute gains on sale; the page is the single source of that detail.
scr_fixed_assets_asset_information_page.ifSkipped: Asset-level questions cannot be answered from the system.
redFlags: Missing source document reference

scr_fixed_assets_transferring_an_asset_t.purpose: Records the move of an asset to another location within the company — e.g., shared maintenance equipment moved between sister properties — transferring cost and accumulated depreciation between locations.
scr_fixed_assets_transferring_an_asset_t.outcome: The asset and its depreciation follow it to the new property's books.
scr_fixed_assets_transferring_an_asset_t.rootCause: When properties are separate legal entities, an asset moved without a transfer leaves one property depreciating equipment it no longer has. Transfers also require intercompany entries when entities differ.
scr_fixed_assets_transferring_an_asset_t.ifSkipped: Assets are reported at the wrong property, and depreciation expense is charged to the wrong owner.
redFlags: Transfers between different owners' entities without a sale or billing

scr_fixed_assets_reclassing_an_asset_to_.purpose: Moves an asset to a different GL account — for example from Building Improvements to FF&E, or out of CIP into the final asset account — when it was classified incorrectly.
scr_fixed_assets_reclassing_an_asset_to_.outcome: Assets sit in the correct balance-sheet accounts, supporting correct presentation and depreciation.
scr_fixed_assets_reclassing_an_asset_to_.rootCause: Capital items are frequently misclassified at invoice entry (appliances coded as building improvements). Classification affects depreciation lives and financial statement presentation.
scr_fixed_assets_reclassing_an_asset_to_.ifSkipped: Balance-sheet asset categories are misstated and depreciation uses the wrong lives.
redFlags: Reclasses that change lives without recalculating depreciation

scr_fixed_assets_draft_assets.purpose: Section explaining draft assets — asset records captured automatically from capital invoices processed by external systems such as OpsTechnology — which wait for activation before they depreciate.
scr_fixed_assets_draft_assets.outcome: Capital invoices feed the register automatically, with a human review before assets go live.
scr_fixed_assets_draft_assets.rootCause: Automating asset creation reduces missed capitalizations, but automated coding can be wrong. The draft stage lets accountants correct class, life and in-service date before depreciation starts.
scr_fixed_assets_draft_assets.ifSkipped: Drafts accumulate unactivated, and capital spend is never depreciated.
redFlags: Drafts older than one close cycle
